$comment: UploadGrant wire format. This IS a wire format, not an API surface: a grant is minted by a server in one language and consumed by a browser client in another, so the JSON key names are part of the cross-SDK contract in the same way the E2EE envelope's byte layout is. The canonical flagship case -- a FastAPI backend and a React frontend -- crosses this boundary on every upload. Key names are camelCase on the wire regardless of the producing language, matching provider-metadata.json's rule.

wire_keys.$comment: Producers MUST emit these names exactly. A Python implementation writes 'expiresAt', not 'expires_at', even though snake_case is idiomatic internally.

absent_optionals.$comment: An optional field that does not apply MUST be omitted, never serialized as null. This is not stylistic. A Python producer emitting "maxBytes": null made the TypeScript browser client reject every upload, because `size > null` coerces null to 0 and evaluates true in JavaScript. Producers omit; consumers must still tolerate null defensively, since other servers exist.

regression.symptom: DirectUploadError: File is 3145728 bytes but this grant allows at most null.

protocol.single: the whole body is sent in one request
protocol.resumable: chunked transfer with Content-Range, survives a dropped connection

url.$comment: The capability itself. Anyone holding it can write to that one path until it expires, so it must never be logged, cached in a URL bar, or embedded in a page served to a user other than the uploader.
url.$comment_secret: For SigV4 the access key ID DOES appear in X-Amz-Credential and that is correct and unavoidable; the secret access key never appears. Do not confuse the two when testing: MinIO's default credentials use the same string for both, which makes a naive substring check report a false leak.

headers.$comment: Headers the client must reproduce verbatim. Prefer empty. Every header signed into an S3 presigned URL becomes one the browser is obliged to send byte-for-byte, and a mismatch is the usual cause of an otherwise-inexplicable 403.

expiresAt.$comment: Failing closed is the only safe reading of a missing bound on a bearer capability. A consumer MUST NOT treat a missing expiry as 'never expires'.

chunkSize.$comment: Only meaningful when protocol is 'resumable'. Google Drive requires every chunk but the last to be a multiple of 256 KiB; a grant carrying a chunkSize that violates its provider's alignment will fail mid-transfer, not at the start.

provider_shapes.$comment: Two providers reach the same shape by different routes. Both produce a URL a browser can write to with no credentials, which is the property that matters.

s3-compatible.mechanism: SigV4 presigned PUT, signing UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD and the host header only
s3-compatible.$comment: The signature covers the object key, so a client cannot redirect the upload to a different path. Verified: editing the key in the URL yields HTTP 403 from the server.

google-drive.mechanism: resumable session URI from the Location header of an initiate call
google-drive.$comment: Drive wants X-Upload-Content-Length when the session opens, and a session opened with the wrong total rejects the final chunk. The session URI needs no Authorization header, which is what keeps the server's OAuth token server-side.

providers_without_direct_upload.webdav: authenticates every request with Basic credentials, so there is no URL a browser can be handed without also handing it the password
providers_without_direct_upload.local: a local path is not reachable by a browser
